insight: Only a trace of rain has fallen recently (0.4 mm) — very little rain, and too little to drive meaningful runoff. Strong summer sunlight is helping disinfect the water. The model's main signals right now: hours since high tide is lowering risk — the timing relative to high tide affects how concentrated bacteria are at the shoreline; only 0.4 mm of rain has fallen — very little rain, not enough to drive meaningful runoff; and seasonal pattern is raising risk — seasonal patterns (wet winters vs dry summers) set the baseline risk. The last lab sample (51 MPN/100mL) is now 9 days old — beaches are sampled about weekly, so a reading this stale carries little weight, and this estimate leans on current conditions. It's a naturally clean, well-flushed open-coast beach (unsafe only ~3% of the time), so outside of storms it's reliably safe.
